claims.claim_vi: Option 1, a Set, is fast but not space-efficient; option 2, storing URLs in a database, works but puts a very high load on the database; option 3, a Bloom filter, is preferred.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: A Bloom filter was proposed by Burton Howard Bloom in 1970; it is a probabilistic data structure that tests whether an element is a member of a set: false means definitely not in the set, true means probably in it; false positives are possible, false negatives are not.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: The basic structure is a bit vector. To add an element, feed it to 3 hash functions (A, B, C) and set the bits at the resulting positions; two different URLs can set the same bit (index 5 in the source image), which is why false positives are possible.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: To test a URL, apply the same hash functions; if all three bits are 1 it may exist, if any is 0 it definitely does not.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Hash functions must be uniformly distributed and fast; RedisBloom and Apache Spark use murmur, InfluxDB uses xxhash.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: Spark describes its Bloom filter as a space-efficient probabilistic data structure with one-sided error: a claim that an item is contained might be wrong, a claim that it is not contained is definitely true; the test method is mightContain.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: In Spark the add path sets the bits at numHashFunctions positions computed as h1 + i * h2 and the test path returns true only if all those bits are set; it does not use independent hash functions per position.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: Spark warns that overflowing a Bloom filter with significantly more elements than expected saturates it and sharply worsens its false positive probability.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: The source gives no bit counts, number of hash functions or false-positive rate; a false positive for a crawler means an unseen address is skipped as if seen.

design_notes_vi: Ba cách, hai chuỗi ba bước (thêm và kiểm tra) và một khung ghi nhớ. Ví dụ chỉ số 5 của ảnh nguồn được nói thành lời, không vẽ lại ảnh. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source has one image; the lesson redraws the three options and the add and test steps as cards and two step sequences and does not use the source image.
The source draws three independent hash functions; the Spark source shows a real filter derives its positions from two hash values (h1 + i * h2). The lesson adds this from the pinned Spark source.
Source says nothing about a filter overfilling; the lesson adds Spark's warning about saturation.
